description: This specification describes the 5-block structure common to all SWIFT MT (Message Type) messages. Every MT message (MT103, MT202, MT940, MT942, etc.) consists of up to 5 blocks wrapped in curly braces. Blocks 1, 2, and 4 are mandatory. Blocks 3 and 5 are optional.

blocks.name: Basic Header
blocks.description: Identifies the application, service, sender, and message sequence. This block is automatically generated by the SWIFT system when the message is sent.

structure.description: Application identifier. Always 'F' for FIN (Financial Application).
Service identifier. '01' = FIN/GPA (General Purpose Application), '21' = FIN/ACK (Acknowledgement).
Sender's BIC (8 characters) + logical terminal code (1 character) + branch code (3 characters). The logical terminal code is typically A-Z for live messages, or X for test messages.

subfields.name: bic
subfields.description: Bank Identifier Code: institution(4) + country(2) + location(2)

subfields.name: logical_terminal
subfields.description: Logical terminal identifier. A-Z for production, X for test.

subfields.name: branch_code
subfields.description: Branch code. XXX for head office.

structure.description: Session number assigned by SWIFT. Four-digit numeric value.
Message sequence number within the session. Six-digit numeric value.

notes: Block 1 is generated by the SWIFT network, not by the sender application
The logical terminal character distinguishes production (A-Z) from test (X) messages
Session and sequence numbers are assigned by SWIFT for message tracking and sequencing

blocks.name: Application Header
blocks.description: Contains message type, priority, delivery information, and either destination (for input) or origination (for output) details. This block differs between input (I) and output (O) messages.

variants.description: Input Application Header - used when sending a message to SWIFT

structure.description: Input/Output identifier. Always 'I' for input messages.
SWIFT message type (e.g., 103, 202, 940, 942)
Receiver's BIC (8 characters) + logical terminal (1 character) + branch code (3 characters)
Message priority. 'N' = Normal, 'U' = Urgent. Urgent messages have higher processing priority and cost more.
Delivery monitoring level (optional). 1=Non-Delivery Warning, 2=Delivery Notification, 3=Both. Omitted if not requested.
Obsolescence period in minutes (optional). After this time, undelivered messages generate a non-delivery notification. '020' = 20 minutes, '003' = 15 minutes (default).

variants.description: Output Application Header - used when receiving a message from SWIFT

structure.description: Input/Output identifier. Always 'O' for output messages.
SWIFT message type (e.g., 103, 202, 940, 942)
Time the message was input to SWIFT by the sender. Format: HHMM (24-hour format)

Message Input Reference (MIR). Contains: input date (YYMMDD) + sender's BIC (12 chars) + session number (4 digits) + sequence number (6 digits). This uniquely identifies the message in the SWIFT network.

subfields.name: input_date
subfields.description: Date message was input. Format: YYMMDD

subfields.name: sender_bic
subfields.description: Sender's full logical terminal address (BIC + logical terminal + branch)

structure.description: Date the message was output from SWIFT to the receiver. Format: YYMMDD
Time the message was output from SWIFT to the receiver. Format: HHMM
Message priority. 'N' = Normal, 'U' = Urgent.

notes: Input messages (I) are sent TO SWIFT, output messages (O) are received FROM SWIFT
The MIR (Message Input Reference) in output messages uniquely identifies every SWIFT message globally
Priority affects both processing speed and cost: urgent messages are more expensive
Delivery monitoring and obsolescence period are optional features for tracking message delivery

blocks.name: User Header
blocks.description: Contains optional user-defined or system-generated tag-value pairs providing additional metadata about the message. Tags are 3-digit or 3-letter codes enclosed in curly braces within the block.

structure.description: One or more tag-value pairs, each enclosed in curly braces. No specific ordering required.

common_tags.name: Banking Priority
common_tags.description: Service type identifier for SWIFT for Corporates (SWIFTNet FIN)
values: TGT - TARGET (Trans-European Automated Real-time Gross Settlement Express Transfer)

common_tags.name: Message User Reference (MUR)
common_tags.description: User-defined reference for tracking and reconciliation. Maximum 16 characters.
common_tags.notes: Often used by corporates for end-to-end tracking of payment instructions

common_tags.name: Service Type Identifier
common_tags.description: Identifies the type of service or message validation

common_tags.name: Banking Priority
common_tags.description: Alternative banking priority code

common_tags.name: Addressee Information
common_tags.description: Routing information for specific addressee handling

common_tags.name: Validation Flag
common_tags.description: Indicates specific validation or processing requirements

common_tags.name: Unique End-to-End Transaction Reference (UETR)
common_tags.description: UUID (RFC 4122) uniquely identifying the payment transaction across the payment chain. Mandatory for SWIFT gpi (Global Payments Innovation) messages.
common_tags.notes: UETR enables end-to-end payment tracking in the SWIFT gpi service. Format is standard UUID with lowercase hex digits and hyphens.

common_tags.name: Payment Controls Information
common_tags.description: Additional payment controls and screening information

common_tags.name: Balance Checkpoint
common_tags.description: Used in MT940/942 messages to indicate balance checkpoint

common_tags.name: Related Reference
common_tags.description: Reference to a related message

common_tags.name: Sanctions Screening Information
common_tags.description: Result of sanctions screening (SWIFT Sanctions Screening)

notes: Block 3 is optional and may be omitted entirely
Tags can appear in any order within the block
Not all tags are applicable to all message types
SWIFT gpi messages require tag 121 (UETR) for end-to-end tracking
Tag 108 (MUR) is commonly used by corporates but not mandatory
Some tags are system-generated by SWIFT, others are user-provided

blocks.name: Text Block
blocks.description: Contains the actual message content as a series of fields in tag-value format. This is the payload of the MT message. Field tags are numeric (2 digits) optionally followed by a letter (e.g., :20:, :32A:, :50K:). Each message type defines which fields are mandatory and optional.

structure.description: Block 4 opening delimiter
CRLF (Carriage Return + Line Feed) separates fields. Each field typically starts on a new line.
Field format: colon + tag (2 digits + optional letter) + colon + value. Multi-line values continue on subsequent lines without a tag prefix.

subcomponents.name: tag
subcomponents.description: Field tag: 2 digits (NN) optionally followed by a letter (a). Examples: :20:, :32A:, :50K:, :59F:

subcomponents.name: value
subcomponents.description: Field value. Can be single-line or multi-line. Multi-line values continue on next line without tag prefix. Character sets vary by field (SWIFT X, Y, or Z).

structure.description: For multi-line field values, subsequent lines do NOT have a tag prefix. They are continuations of the previous field.
Block 4 closing: CRLF + dash + closing brace

field_tag_format.description: Field tags consist of 2 digits optionally followed by a single uppercase letter

field_options.description: Many fields have multiple options indicated by a letter suffix (A, B, C, D, F, K, etc.). Each option represents a different format for the same logical field. Exactly one option must be present.

examples.name: Ordering Institution
options: 52D - Name and address with optional account

character_sets.description: Different fields allow different character sets as defined by SWIFT

sets.name: Basic alphanumeric
sets.description: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, space, and limited punctuation: / - ? : ( ) . , ' +
sets.usage: Most basic fields like references, codes

sets.name: Uppercase and numbers with extended punctuation
Extended character set
sets.description: Character set X plus additional special characters including CRLF
sets.usage: Free-format text fields like remittance information

examples.description: Simple MT103 Block 4 with single-line fields

examples.content:
{4:
:20:REF123456
:50K:/DE89370400440532013000
JOHN DOE
123 MAIN STREET
NEW YORK NY 10001
US
:59:/GB29NWBK60161331926819
JANE SMITH
456 HIGH STREET
LONDON
:70:INVOICE 2023-1234
PAYMENT FOR SERVICES
-}

notes: Block 4 contains the actual business data of the message
Field tags are defined per message type (MT103, MT202, MT940, MT942, etc.)
CRLF (\r\n) is the line separator, not just LF (\n)
Multi-line field values continue without a tag prefix on subsequent lines
Field ordering is significant: some fields must appear in a specific sequence
Option letters (A, B, C, D, F, K) distinguish different formats for the same logical field
Character set restrictions vary by field and are enforced during validation
The dash before the closing brace must be on its own line preceded by CRLF

blocks.name: Trailer
blocks.description: Contains optional system-generated or user-defined trailer information such as checksums, duplicate detection, security, and testing markers. Like Block 3, it uses tag-value pairs enclosed in curly braces.

structure.description: One or more tag-value pairs, each enclosed in curly braces. Tags are 3-letter codes.

common_tags.name: Checksum
common_tags.description: Message authentication checksum calculated by SWIFT. 12 hexadecimal characters.
common_tags.notes: Generated by SWIFT for message integrity verification. Cannot be user-supplied.

common_tags.name: Training
common_tags.description: Indicates this is a training message, not a live production message. No value required.
common_tags.notes: Presence of this tag marks the message for training purposes. Must be absent in production.

common_tags.name: Possible Duplicate Emission
common_tags.description: Indicates the message might be a duplicate of a previously sent message. Contains date/time of possible original.
common_tags.notes: Used when the sender is uncertain if a previous transmission was successful

common_tags.name: Possible Duplicate Message
common_tags.description: Similar to PDE but set by SWIFT system when it detects potential duplication

common_tags.name: Delayed Message
common_tags.description: Indicates message was delayed in the SWIFT network. Contains reason code.
common_tags.notes: System-generated when message delivery is delayed beyond normal processing time

common_tags.name: Message Reference
common_tags.description: Reference to original message in case of queries or cancellations. Contains MIR of referenced message.
common_tags.notes: Used in MT192, MT196, MT199 (free format message) to reference original payment message

common_tags.name: System Originated
common_tags.description: Indicates the message was generated by a SWIFT system component, not a user application
common_tags.notes: Common in acknowledgements and system notifications

common_tags.name: Message Authentication Code
common_tags.description: Authentication code for bilateral key exchange security
common_tags.notes: Used in bilateral agreements for additional message authentication

common_tags.name: Proprietary Authentication Code
common_tags.description: User-defined authentication code for additional security
common_tags.notes: Allows institutions to add proprietary security checks

common_tags.name: Supplementary Authentication Code
common_tags.description: Additional authentication for enhanced security
common_tags.notes: Used in conjunction with MAC for multi-layer authentication

common_tags.name: Information for Receiving Institution
common_tags.description: Additional information for the receiver not part of the message text

notes: Block 5 is optional and may be omitted entirely
Most tags in Block 5 are system-generated by SWIFT, not user-provided
CHK (checksum) is the most common tag and is always generated by SWIFT
TNG (training) tag must NEVER appear in production messages
Duplicate detection tags (PDE, PDM) help prevent processing the same payment twice
Authentication tags (MAC, PAC, SAC) are used for bilateral security arrangements
Tags can appear in any order within the block

message_structure.description: Complete MT message structure with all blocks
rules: Blocks 3 and 5 are optional and may be omitted
Each block is self-contained within curly braces {...}
No whitespace between blocks (except within Block 4 text content)
Block delimiters use curly braces { } with no spaces

complete_example.description: Complete MT103 message with all 5 blocks

explanation.block1: F01 = FIN, DEUTDEFFAXXX = sender (Deutsche Bank Frankfurt), 1234567890 = session/sequence
explanation.block2: I103 = input MT103, BNPAFRPPAXXX = receiver (BNP Paribas Paris), N = normal priority (omitted here for brevity)
explanation.block3: MUR reference and UETR for tracking
explanation.block4: Transaction reference, bank op code, value date/currency/amount, ordering customer, beneficiary, charges

character_encoding.description: SWIFT messages use a specific character encoding
notes: SWIFT does not support full Unicode or UTF-8
Non-ASCII characters must be transliterated (e.g., ü -> ue, é -> e)
Block delimiters use curly braces { }
Field delimiters in Block 4 use colon :
CRLF is mandatory for line breaks within Block 4, not just LF

validation_rules.description: General validation rules that apply to all MT messages

rules.description: Blocks must appear in sequence: 1, 2, [3], 4, [5] where [3] and [5] are optional
Blocks 1, 2, and 4 must always be present
All BIC codes (in blocks 1, 2, and fields) must conform to ISO 9362 format
Message type in Block 2 must match the fields present in Block 4
Field values must only contain characters from the allowed SWIFT character set for that field
When a field has multiple options (A/B/D/K), exactly one option must be present
Block 4 must use CRLF (\r\n) for line separators, not LF alone
Test messages must have 'X' in logical terminal position (Block 1, position 12) and may have {TNG:} in Block 5
